info.title: Bravado Trade API
info.description:
Consolidated order execution API for Bravado partners (v2). One high-level
order endpoint replaces the v1 limit/market/advanced split, plus native
position redeem, split/merge, pUSD withdraw, and managed-strategy admin.
`/v1/trade/*` remains available and unchanged — v2 is additive.

Auth, idempotency, rate-limit, numeric-as-string and timestamp conventions
are identical to v1 (see the v1 spec), except every path is under
`/v2/trade`. Errors are spelled out here rather than deferred, because a
client generated from this document alone would otherwise never learn that
the header exists:

* **Errors** use the shape `{"error": "...", "code": "...",
"request_id": "..."}` with an appropriate non-2xx HTTP status. The
`code` is a stable enum (see error catalog).
* **Every error answered by a Trade API route also carries the code in
the `X-Bravado-Error-Code`** response header — a request that never reached
one has neither the header nor a `code`, and there are four ways to miss:
a path outside these prefixes, a refused CORS preflight, a request refused
below the HTTP framework (the 45s read timeout, a malformed request line,
oversized headers), or a reply from the platform edge. Prefer the
header over parsing the body on 5xx: our hosting
platform replaces the body of any 5xx with its own HTML error page, so the
JSON envelope does not reach you for codes like `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`,
`RUNNER_UNHEALTHY` or `IDEMPOTENCY_INDETERMINATE`. Headers survive intact,
and `x-do-orig-status` carries the real status.

Endpoints:
* `POST /v2/trade/order` — single consolidated order. `type` =
  `LIMIT | MARKET | PEGGED | TWAP | ICEBERG | TAKE_PROFIT | STOP_LOSS |
  TRAILING_STOP | TRAILING_BUY`. Optional `take_profit` / `stop_loss`
  brackets attach to a
  LIMIT/MARKET buy entry (best-effort). Managed strategies (PEGGED / TWAP /
  ICEBERG / STOP_LOSS / TRAILING_STOP / TRAILING_BUY) return a `record_id`
  instead of an
  `order_id`.
* `GET /v2/trade/strategies` + `DELETE /v2/trade/strategies/{record_id}` —
  list and cancel managed strategies (see the guide below).
* `POST /v2/trade/positions/redeem` — redeem a resolved position to pUSD;
  `/positions/split` and `/positions/merge` — on-chain CTF split/merge.
* `POST /v2/trade/withdraw` — withdraw pUSD to an external address. Requires
  the dedicated `trade.withdraw` scope (not granted by `trade.execute`).
* `POST /v2/trade/combo/quote|accept|redeem` + `GET /v2/trade/combo/positions`
  — multi-leg RFQ parlays (Combos). Quote → accept within ~8.5s → manual
  redeem. Requires the dedicated `trade.combos` scope.
* Reads (`account`, `balances`, `positions`, `orders/open`, `activity`),
  cancels, and user provisioning are the same as v1, mounted under
  `/v2/trade`.

Tags:
* `trade.health` — liveness probe and OpenAPI spec.
* `trade.read` — account, balances, positions, open orders, activity,
  strategies.
* `trade.execute` — consolidated order placement + position redeem.
* `trade.cancel` — single, batch, cancel-all, and strategy cancel.
* `trade.withdraw` — pUSD withdrawals to external addresses.
* `trade.combos` — multi-leg RFQ parlay quote/accept/redeem + positions.
* `trade.users` — provision integration users (white-label flow).

All endpoints return `application/json`.


## Advanced orders — correct payloads (`POST /v2/trade/order`)

Most integration bugs come from **units** — read this table first.

| Field | Unit | Example | NOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price`, `take_profit.price`, `stop_loss.price`, `price_floor`, `price_ceiling`, `execution.trailing_offset`, `execution.high_water_mark`, `execution.low_water_mark` | **decimal probability** 0.001–0.999 | `"0.60"` (= 60¢) | ❌ cents `"60"` |
| `size`, `execution.clip_size`, bracket `size` | **shares** | `"100"` | — |
| `budget_usdc`, `quote_amount` | **US dollars** | `"50"` | ❌ micro-units |
| `offset_ticks` | CLOB ticks (1 tick = 0.1¢) | `0` | — |
| `execution.trailing_offset_pct`, `execution.randomize_pct`, `execution.price_tolerance_pct` | percent 0–100 | `5` | — |
| `execution.duration_sec`, `execution.interval_sec` | seconds (interval ≥ 10) | `3600`, `60` | — |

All field names are **snake_case**. Send a `price` of `72` and you'll get
`price must be a decimal probability 0.001–0.999; received 72 — did you mean 0.72?`.
Every mutating request needs an `Idempotency-Key` header.

### LIMIT / MARKET (with optional protective brackets)

```jsonc
// Limit buy at 62¢ for 100 shares, with a take-profit and a partial stop-loss
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "LIMIT",
  "price": "0.62", "size": "100",
  "take_profit": { "price": "0.72" },              // whole entry by default
  "stop_loss":   { "price": "0.55", "size": "50" } // positive size = partial
}
// Bracket size: omitted OR "0" = the whole entry.
// Market buy = USD to spend; market sell = shares
{ "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "MARKET", "quote_amount": "10" }
{ "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "sell", "type": "MARKET", "size": "100" }
```

Brackets attach only to a **buy** LIMIT/MARKET entry, best-effort: the entry
still succeeds if a bracket fails. **Always inspect the response** — a failed
bracket is reported at `brackets.take_profit.error` / `brackets.stop_loss.error`
AND surfaced in a top-level `warnings: [...]`.

### PEGGED

```jsonc
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "PEGGED",
  "outcome": "yes", "offset_ticks": 0,
  "budget_usdc": "50",                          // dollars, > 0 (snake_case)
  "price_floor": 0.05, "price_ceiling": 0.95,   // optional decimals
  "condition_id": "0x…"
}
```

`budget_usdc` is required (`quote_amount` is accepted as an alias — the same
dollar field a MARKET buy uses).

### ICEBERG

```jsonc
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "ICEBERG",
  "price": "0.62", "size": "1000",
  "execution": { "clip_size": "50", "price_tolerance_pct": 5 }
}
```

Each slice must be **≥ $1 in notional** (`clip_size × price ≥ 1`) and
`clip_size < size`. Slices are **post-only** — price the iceberg passively
(at or below the bid for a buy); at/above the ask it is rejected with
`order crosses book`.

### TWAP

```jsonc
// Fully explicit
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "TWAP",
  "price": "0.62", "size": "1000",
  "execution": { "duration_sec": 3600, "interval_sec": 60 }
}
// Market-style: dollars only — price derived from the live top of book
// (best ask for a buy, best bid for a sell); size = quote_amount / price
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "TWAP",
  "quote_amount": "5",
  "execution": { "duration_sec": 60, "interval_sec": 10 }
}
```

`interval_sec` (≥ 10) and `duration_sec` are required, plus **either** `size`
(shares) **or** `quote_amount` (dollars). `price` is optional — when omitted
the derived limit is echoed in the response `message`. The derived price is a
**limit**: slices never chase past it. `duration_sec` must be **strictly
greater** than `interval_sec` — a one-slice TWAP is a plain limit order and is
refused.

`clip_size` and `randomize_pct` are **rejected** with `INVALID_BODY`: a TWAP
slices on a clock, so a clip size cannot be honoured. They used to be accepted
and dropped with a `warnings` entry, which told nobody. Use `ICEBERG` to
control the size of each clip — `clip_size` is required there and unaffected.

### TRAILING_STOP

```jsonc
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "sell", "type": "TRAILING_STOP",
  "size": "100",
  "execution": {
    "trailing_offset_pct": 5,        // the trail distance
    "high_water_mark": "0.60"        // current market price as the reference
  }
}
```

Requires `size` + an offset (`trailing_offset_pct` **or** `trailing_offset`)
+ a reference (`execution.high_water_mark` or top-level `price`).

### TRAILING_BUY

The entry mirror of TRAILING_STOP. A trailing stop follows the price up and
sells when it falls back by your offset; a trailing buy follows the ask down
and buys when it bounces back up by your offset. Use it to enter on a dip
without having to pick the bottom.

```jsonc
{
  "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "buy", "type": "TRAILING_BUY",
  "quote_amount": "50",              // US DOLLARS to spend, not shares
  "execution": {
    "trailing_offset_pct": 5,        // the bounce that triggers the entry
    "low_water_mark": "0.40",        // optional starting reference
    "price_ceiling": "0.55"          // optional hard cap
  }
}
```

Requires `quote_amount` + an offset (`trailing_offset_pct` **or**
`trailing_offset`). It takes dollars rather than shares because the share
count is not known until the entry price is.

`low_water_mark` is optional: omit it and the engine seeds the reference from
the first ask it sees, which is what you want when arming at the current market.

`price_ceiling` is a veto, not a trigger. If the ask gaps straight past it the
entry does not fire at any price, and the order stays armed in case a cheaper
ask comes back. A ceiling below the entry your offset implies is rejected at
arm time, since it could never fire.

### TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS (standalone, on an existing position)

```jsonc
{ "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "sell", "type": "TAKE_PROFIT", "price": "0.72", "size": "50" }
{ "symbol": "<token_id>", "side": "sell", "type": "STOP_LOSS",  "price": "0.55", "size": "50" }
```

These SELL shares you already hold — `size` is checked against your **share**
balance (not pUSD): `Not enough shares to place this sell — holding X…`.

### Market microstructure constraints (rejections that are NOT bugs)

- Resting orders have a **per-market share minimum** (usually 5).
- Market orders have a **$1 minimum amount**.
- Iceberg slices are **post-only** (see ICEBERG above).

### Tracking & canceling managed strategies

"Where do I see my iceberg / trailing stop?" — **`GET /v2/trade/strategies`**
lists every partner-created TWAP / ICEBERG / PEGGED / STOP_LOSS /
TRAILING_STOP; `DELETE /v2/trade/strategies/{record_id}` cancels one.

- The `record_id` returned by `POST /v2/trade/order` is the id to track/cancel.
- Pre-trigger stop-losses and trailing stops exist **only** in this list; they
  appear on `/orders/open` (`is_stop_loss: true`) only after the runner
  triggers them into a real CLOB order.
- **`price` is not the fill.** On a STOP_LOSS or TRAILING_STOP it is the level
  the order was armed at, and on a TRAILING_BUY it is the ceiling. The price the
  order actually got is `executed_price`, with `filled_size` alongside it.
  Both are null until it executes. Showing `price` as the exit makes every
  trailing stop look like it closed exactly where it opened.
- An iceberg's working slice IS a live CLOB order and also shows on
  `/orders/open`; the parent totals live in the strategy record.
- Standalone TAKE_PROFIT places a real CLOB sell immediately — it lives on
  `/orders/open` (`is_take_profit: true`), not in the strategies list.
- A stop-loss can be canceled only while untriggered; once executing, cancel
  the resulting order via `DELETE /v2/trade/orders/{order_id}`.

### Response conventions

- **Managed strategies** return `record_id` + `status: "PENDING" | "ACTIVE"`
  plus a `message` — `PENDING` is **not** a rejection.
- **CLOB orders** (LIMIT / MARKET / TAKE_PROFIT) return `order_id`.
- Check `warnings: string[]` on every response — a `200` can still carry
  "entry OK, but the take-profit didn't place because …".
- On `429`, respect `Retry-After` instead of retrying immediately.



## Combos — multi-leg RFQ parlays (`/v2/trade/combo/*`)

A **combo** is a single position that pays out only if **every** leg wins — a
parlay. Unlike a normal order it is priced by **request-for-quote (RFQ)**: you
ask for a quote, then accept it within a short window. Requires the dedicated
**`trade.combos`** scope.

The lifecycle is three calls (accept is money-moving and on-chain):

`quote` → `accept` (within ~8.5s) → *(after the event resolves)* `redeem`

### Units — read this first

| Field | Unit | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `leg_position_ids` | 2–10 **YES position ids** (one per leg) | `["7248…", "9931…"]` |
| `notional_usd` | **US dollars** the user spends (BUY) | `5` |
| `price_cents` (response) | cents per blended YES share | `2` (= $0.02) |
| `maker_amount_usd` (response) | dollars the maker posts | `1.2` |
| `taker_shares` (response) | combo shares received | `66.5` |
| `payout_usd` (redeem response) | pUSD paid out for winning shares | `50` |

Field names are **snake_case**. Every mutating request needs an
`Idempotency-Key` header. Only **`BUY`** is supported (there is no combo sell —
exit is redeem-on-win or let it resolve to $0).

### 1) Quote — `POST /v2/trade/combo/quote`

```jsonc
{
  "leg_position_ids": ["<yes_position_id_A>", "<yes_position_id_B>"],
  "notional_usd": 5            // dollars to spend
  // "side": "BUY"             // optional; BUY is the only value
}
```

Returns the priced quote:

```jsonc
{
  "combo_order_id": "…",       // pass both of these to /accept
  "quote_id": "…",
  "rfq_id": "…",
  "price_cents": 2,
  "maker_amount_usd": 1.2,
  "taker_shares": 66.5,
  "expires_at": "2026-07-17T15:04:05.000Z"   // ISO — accept BEFORE this
}
```

The quote is valid **~8.5 seconds**. It is a real maker RFQ, not an estimate —
don't cache it.

### 2) Accept — `POST /v2/trade/combo/accept`

```jsonc
{ "combo_order_id": "…", "quote_id": "…" }
```

```jsonc
{ "combo_order_id": "…", "status": "EXECUTED", "transaction_hash": "0x…" }
```

Accept signs and submits on-chain. It must land **before `expires_at`** — a
stale accept returns **`410 QUOTE_EXPIRED`**. On expiry, **re-quote and accept
the fresh quote** — never blind-retry the same accept: the price may have moved
(same lesson as any RFQ). Idempotency-Key protects against double-submit of the
*same* accept, not against re-pricing.

### 3) Redeem — `POST /v2/trade/combo/redeem`

A combo does **not** auto-settle to cash. After the event resolves in your
favor, claim it manually:

```jsonc
{ "combo_order_id": "…" }          // or { "combo_position_id": "…" } from /positions
```

```jsonc
{ "combo_order_id": "…", "status": "REDEEMED", "payout_usd": 50, "transaction_hash": "0x…" }
```

Only a **`RESOLVED_WIN`** combo pays out — one losing leg zeroes the whole
combo (that is a correct parlay result, not a bug). Redeem before resolution or
on a losing combo is rejected.

### 4) Positions — `GET /v2/trade/combo/positions`

Lists the bound user's combo positions. Filters:
`status` = `OPEN | PARTIAL | RESOLVED_WIN | RESOLVED_LOSS`, plus `limit`
(≤ 500) and `offset`. Use the returned position id as `combo_position_id` for
redeem.

### Rejections that are NOT bugs

- **`410 QUOTE_EXPIRED`** — accept came after `expires_at`. Re-quote.
- **`422 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`** — the wallet can't cover `notional_usd` **plus
  the fee**. The message states the dollars needed and the largest affordable
  notional; size the combo a little under the balance.
- **`422 NO_LIQUIDITY` / no maker** — no counterparty quoted the legs right now
  (common on thin/near-event markets). Retry, or reduce `notional_usd`.

get.description: Returns ok+ts when the partner-api module is reachable. Public; no auth.
Returns the OpenAPI 3 spec for /v1/trade endpoints (tags trade.*). Public; no auth.  Admin routes are excluded — they are internal-only.

Returns the integration, binding, api key, wallet (EOA + Safe), and the builder code resolved for this key. Useful as the first call after onboarding to verify credentials and inspect quotas. onboarding_status is per venue: with ?venue=predictfun — or under /v2/trade/predictfun/account — it reports predict.fun readiness instead of the Polygon pUSD allowance. Addresses here are chain-specific: safe_address is the Polymarket proxy on Polygon, while predict.fun collateral (USDT-BEP20 on BNB Chain) must be sent to the EOA instead. Read the safe_address field description before building a deposit flow.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list. On this endpoint it selects which venue's onboarding_status is reported; the wallet block is unchanged and still describes the Polymarket accounts.

eoa_address.description: The end user's externally owned account — a keypair, so the same value on every EVM chain. Carries no chain because it needs none. Do not build a deposit flow from this field: use venues[], where each address comes with the chain and assets it accepts.

safe_address.description: Addresses are chain-specific. safe_address identifies the user's Polymarket proxy on Polygon, and is NULL whenever the requested venue does not trade through a Safe — on predict.fun it is always null, because that venue trades from the EOA and no Safe exists there. Never use it as a deposit address for predict.fun: that collateral is USDT-BEP20 on BNB Chain and goes to the EOA. Bravado does not support recovery of funds sent to safe_address on BNB Chain, and recovery may be impossible; design your flow on the assumption that the loss is final. Prefer venues[] over this field — it labels every address with its chain.

chain.description: The chain these addresses are reported for — the requested venue's chain. Here so this block is machine-readable on its own: a client that never reads venues[] still cannot pair an address with the wrong network. It labels the context, not the keypair — eoa_address is the same account on every EVM chain, and this says which one these fields are answering about.

protocol_v2_status.description: Polymarket Protocol V2 markets only, and present only while Bravado trades them. Whether the user's wallet holds the ExchangeV3 approvals a V2 order needs: `ready`; `pending` — the first V2 order sets them (that order may need one retry), v1 trading is unaffected; `unknown` — the chain could not be read. Never gate v1 trading on it: `onboarding_status` is still the readiness to trade.

venue.description: polymarket | predictfun

name.description: Human name, e.g. Polygon, BNB Smart Chain

trading_address.description: The address that trades on this venue. Null when it has not been derived yet — treat null as 'not ready', never as an empty address.

address_type.description: safe_proxy is a contract, deployed on this entry's chain; eoa is a keypair the user controls, which is the same account on any EVM chain. Machine-readable on purpose: for an eoa the same address elsewhere is the same user, while for a safe_proxy Bravado makes no claim about the same address on another chain — do not assume it is the user's, and do not send funds there.

address.description: Where the user funds this venue, on this entry's chain. Null when no address has been derived yet. Bravado does not support recovery of funds sent for this venue on any other chain.

contract.description: ERC20 contract, or null for the chain's native coin.

role.description: collateral funds trading; gas funds the wallet's own transactions. On an EOA-direct venue the wallet pays for its own approvals and orders, so including gas in the deposit avoids waiting on Bravado's top-up.

suggested_minimum.description: For gas, an amount worth sending in one go. Null for collateral, where the right amount is whatever the user intends to trade.

venues.description: One entry per venue this partner may trade on, each self-contained: where to send money, on which chain, in which assets, and whether the user is ready there. Build deposit flows from this, not from the legacy wallet block — that block cannot express more than one chain.

get.description: Returns the user's positions sourced from the Polymarket data-api, normalised to snake_case with numeric fields encoded as JSON strings. Use `?status=active` (default) for currently-held positions with a live mark price and on-chain ERC1155 enrichment, or `?status=closed` for fully-sold positions with realized PnL only (live-only fields like size/current_value/mergeable are zeroed). Each row carries a `status` discriminator for clarity when sources are mixed downstream.

parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list.

get.description: Returns the user's activity timeline. On polymarket, sourced from the Polymarket data-api: trades (BUY/SELL), redemptions, liquidity rewards, maker rebates, referral rewards, splits, merges, conversions, deposits and withdrawals. On venue predictfun the feed carries FILLS ONLY, plus the withdrawals Bravado executed and recorded, which are merged from our own ledger — deposits, redemptions, splits and merges are still unavailable there. Deposit and withdrawal rows name the chain in `network`. Pagination via opaque cursor.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Activity type filter. `WITHDRAW` is DEPRECATED — it is accepted as an alias for `WITHDRAWAL` and will be removed in a future version. Responses always use `WITHDRAWAL`.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list.

network.description: Chain the movement happened on, for deposit and withdrawal rows: `polygon` (chain id 137) for polymarket, `bsc` (56) for predictfun. Absent on market activity. Resolve `transaction_hash` on this chain.

log_index.description: Index of this row's transfer inside `transaction_hash`. A single transaction can move funds for several wallets, so the hash alone does not identify the row. `null` means we could not read the receipt; it is never a guess. Deposit and withdrawal rows only.

counterparty.description: The other address in this row's transfer — who paid a deposit, or who was paid by a withdrawal. Evidence for reconciliation: whether an arrival is new money or your own funds returning is not decidable from one transaction, so we name the counterparty rather than guess. `null` when the receipt could not be read.

source.description: Provenance of this row. Present on rows Bravado records itself; absent on rows sourced from the venue's public activity feed. `backfill` implies transaction_hash is null.

get.description: Returns the bound user's collateral, as JSON strings with 6-decimal precision. On polymarket: pUSD (active V2 collateral) and USDC.e (legacy, wrappable), held by the Polymarket Safe wallet. On venue predictfun: USDT on BNB Chain, held by the EOA and reported in the pusd field, with usdc_e always 0. The number is correct; the field name is legacy.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list.

pusd.description: On polymarket, pUSD held by the Polymarket Safe wallet. On venue predictfun this field carries USDT on BNB Chain, held by the EOA — not pUSD, and not the Safe. The number is correct; the field name is legacy.

get.description:
Open CLOB orders for the bound user, optionally filtered by ?token_id.

**Some of these orders are not yours.** A TWAP, iceberg or pegged record is worked by a runner that posts ordinary orders to the book, and they appear here like any other. `is_twap`, `is_iceberg` and `is_pegged` mark them, and `parent_strategy_id` names the record that owns each one — the id DELETE /v2/trade/strategies/{id} takes.

Do not key an "orders I placed" set on the order_id a placement returned: a strategy placement has no order_id to give, because the record exists before any order does. Filter on parent_strategy_id instead.

is_take_profit and is_stop_loss reflect the same kind of join: TP at creation, SL post-trigger (executionOrderId). Pre-trigger SLs are correctly excluded since they have no live CLOB order until fired.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list.

created_at.description: Unix seconds. The venue's creation time when it reports one; otherwise (always on predictfun) the time the order was placed through this API. 0 = no record of this order being placed through this API (placed elsewhere, or a bid-ladder rung after the first until api#1390). Never 1970.

is_twap.description: True when this order is a slice a TWAP runner is working.

is_iceberg.description: True when this order is a clip an iceberg runner is working.

parent_strategy_id.description: The managed record that owns this order (TWAP / iceberg / pegged), or null when you placed it yourself. This is the id DELETE /v2/trade/strategies/{id} takes — cancel the strategy, not the clip: cancelling a clip cancels the record that owned it.

condition_id.description: The market's condition id — the same value /positions reports, and the key to join the two.

question.description: The market's question as Gamma words it. Note /positions carries a `title` from Polymarket's data-api instead: same market, two upstreams, so the WORDING can differ. Join on condition_id, not on the text.

outcome.description: Which side of the market this token is (e.g. "Yes"), derived from the token's position in the market's outcome list.

title.description: The market's name. Same string as `question` when it comes from the catalogue; a separate key because /positions and /activity already call it `title` and a client joining those surfaces should not have to learn two names.

outcome_index.description: Which outcome this token is, by position in the market's outcome list — the index `outcome` was read from.

event_slug.description: The event this market belongs to, when the catalogue knows it.

venue.description: The venue this market was resolved on. Present so a client never has to infer it from the request it made.

market.description: Which market this order is on. NULL MEANS UNRESOLVED, never 'this token has no market': a market-data outage, an unknown token, and a venue we cannot look up all report null, and the order itself is unaffected either way. Resolved on BOTH venues from the market catalogue we index, so a predictfun order is named like a polymarket one. post.description: Single high-level order endpoint. `type` = LIMIT | MARKET | PEGGED | TWAP | ICEBERG. Optional `take_profit` / `stop_loss` brackets attach to a LIMIT/MARKET buy entry (placed after the entry; best-effort — a failing bracket is reported, not rolled back). Idempotency-Key required.

See the Venues section for the supported list. On predictfun this endpoint accepts LIMIT, MARKET, TWAP and ICEBERG, and requires the partner venue entitlement.

symbol.description: Venue-native outcome token id — a decimal string on both venues. Constrained because it is interpolated into a market lookup: an id carrying query syntax was measured turning that lookup into a different question and returning an unrelated market (#973).

price.description: Decimal probability 0..1, e.g. "0.72" for 72¢ (NOT cents). Required for LIMIT / ICEBERG / TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS. Optional for TWAP (derived from the live top of book when omitted) and TRAILING_STOP (reference; execution.high_water_mark also works).

size.description: Shares. Required for LIMIT / ICEBERG / TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS / TRAILING_STOP and MARKET sell; for TWAP either size or quote_amount works.

quote_amount.description: US dollars. MARKET buy notional; TWAP: shares are derived from it at the limit price; PEGGED: accepted as an alias for budget_usdc.

time_in_force.description: LIMIT only. GTC (default) rests on the book (GTD when expiration is set). IOC fills whatever crosses immediately and cancels the remainder (Polymarket FAK) — the response reports the actual filled_size. FOK fills the full size instantly or cancels entirely. Incompatible with expiration. ON MARKET: a MARKET order is always FAK, so `IOC` is accepted and changes nothing, while `GTC` and `FOK` are REJECTED with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than silently ignored — neither can be honoured (a MARKET order never rests, and it is not all-or-nothing). PREDICTFUN: on a LIMIT only GTC, the default, is accepted; IOC and FOK are VENUE_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. On a MARKET, IOC is accepted there too: the venue cancels a MARKET that does not fill at the touch.

slippage_bps.description: MARKET only. How far from the top of book this order may fill, in basis points (100 = 1%). THE DEFAULT DIFFERS BY VENUE: 300 on polymarket, 100 on predictfun — same field, same 1-5000 range, so omitting it gives you a 3x tighter bound on predictfun. Send the value explicitly if you want one number across venues. The reference is the touch at submit time: the best BID for a sell, the best ASK for a buy — so on a sell it is a price FLOOR, and on a buy a price CEILING. Orders are FAK: the book fills what it can within the bound and the remainder is cancelled, so a partial fill is normal and `filled_size` reports what actually traded. If NOTHING fills within the bound the order is rejected with SLIPPAGE_EXCEEDED (422) and nothing trades — that is a race (the book emptied between our read and the match), not the ordinary outcome. Raising this widens your exposure; it cannot be disabled.

expiration.description: LIMIT and ICEBERG only. Unix seconds; 0 or omitted means GTC. Any other type (MARKET, TWAP, PEGGED, brackets, trailing) rejects it with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than accepting and ignoring it. Must be at least 10s in the future, and no later than 4102444800 (the GTC sentinel) — a larger value is what milliseconds look like where seconds were asked for; both fail with INVALID_BODY. The two types enforce it differently and the difference is worth designing around: on LIMIT the timestamp is signed INTO the order and enforced by the venue, so it holds exactly and even if we are unreachable. On ICEBERG it is a deadline for the STRATEGY, enforced by our runner on its next poll — the record is canceled and its live clip pulled shortly AFTER the timestamp, not at it.

condition_id.description: Optional. Omit it and we resolve the market from `symbol`. An EMPTY string used to be accepted and then failed every lookup silently, so the shape is pinned rather than merely non-empty.

offset_ticks.description: PEGGED: distance from the touch in CLOB ticks (1 tick = $0.001); 0 = passive at the touch.

budget_usdc.description: PEGGED buy budget in US dollars, top-level decimal string, e.g. "50". quote_amount is accepted as an alias.

price_floor.description: Decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (NOT cents). Two uses. PEGGED: the lowest price the runner will chase down to. TWAP SELL with no `price`: the limit every clip is priced against, so each clip fills at max(live touch, this) instead of being pinned to the touch at placement. With `execution.passive: true` a clip rests one tick INSIDE the touch (bestBid + tick), so that formula is off by a tick — the promise that we never cross your number holds in both modes, the arithmetic is exact only in the default one. Snapped protectively — a floor ceils to the cent above, never below your number. WHEN IT IS ACTING AS THE LIMIT it is also what your notional cap is measured against: the cap is `price x size` with no side branch, so a floor bounds a sell exactly as a ceiling bounds a buy. Send an explicit `price` and the cap is measured against that instead.

price_ceiling.description: Decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (NOT cents). Two uses. PEGGED: the highest price the runner will chase up to. TWAP BUY with no `price`: the limit every clip is priced against, so each clip fills at min(live touch, this) instead of being pinned to the touch at placement. With `execution.passive: true` a clip rests one tick INSIDE the touch (bestAsk - tick), so that formula is off by a tick — the promise that we never cross your number holds in both modes, the arithmetic is exact only in the default one. Snapped protectively — a ceiling floors to the cent below, never above your number. WHEN IT IS ACTING AS THE LIMIT it is also what your notional cap is measured against, since `size x ceiling` is the most the order can then spend — so an open ceiling consumes cap. Send an explicit `price` and the cap is measured against that instead.

duration_sec.description: TWAP total run length in seconds

passive.description: TWAP slice style. Default false: each slice takes the touch (buy at the best ask, sell at the best bid), never past your price, so it executes. True: rest one tick inside the touch and never cross — cheaper when it fills, but often it does not. Use it on long horizons.

low_water_mark.description: TRAILING_BUY starting reference price (decimal). Omit to let the engine seed it from the first ask it sees, which is what you want when arming at the current market.

price_ceiling.description: TRAILING_BUY ONLY. Hard cap, decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (`0.0` and `0.00` are zero, and are refused): if the ask gaps past it the entry does not fire at any price and the order stays armed for a cheaper ask. A TWAP reads price_ceiling at the TOP LEVEL of the order, not here — sending it inside `execution` on a TWAP is rejected with INVALID_BODY rather than ignored.

price_floor.description: NOT USED HERE, and rejected. A TWAP SELL reads price_floor at the TOP LEVEL of the order. This field exists only so that sending it in the wrong place fails loudly instead of being dropped.

quote_amount.description: NOT USED HERE, and rejected. MARKET buy, TWAP and PEGGED all read quote_amount at the TOP LEVEL of the order. This field exists only so that sending it in the wrong place fails loudly instead of being dropped.

status.description: The venue's word for the order when it was accepted. ALWAYS PRESENT: the empty string "" is the documented UNKNOWN (a predict.fun LIMIT: the venue's acceptance does not say whether it matched), not a missing field. Test === "", not truthiness. On a MARKET: "matched" = filled in full; "partially_filled" = filled, but at least 0.01 shares (sell) or $0.01 (buy) short of the request, the rest cancelled and nothing resting. A SUCCESS, not an error: treat it as one if you allow-list "matched" (added in #1396). "pending" (predict.fun MARKET) = the venue had not reported the fill when we answered; the final state can arrive later. Not a cancel and not a zero fill: do not place it again (#1412).

filled_size.description: Shares matched at acceptance. "" = UNKNOWN (a predict.fun LIMIT, whose acceptance carries no fill, and a predict.fun MARKET answered "pending"), never zero: reading "" as 0 or as absent is wrong. Reconcile from /orders/open or your fills.

remaining_size.description: What rests after acceptance. "" = UNKNOWN, same rule as filled_size.

planned_at.description: Unix seconds this clip is PLANNED for: clip 1 at created_at, clip k at created_at + (k-1) * interval_sec. Nominal — the runner places each clip on the first poll tick at or after its due time and never catches up, so later clips run late by the accumulated latency.

planned_size.description: Shares this clip is PLANNED at. Nominal: the runner re-sizes every clip from what is left and the time left, so late ticks and resting clips change later sizes and can merge the last clips. Reconcile fills through /orders/open and GET /v2/trade/strategies.

clip_plan.description: TWAP ONLY — absent on every other type, so its presence says the placement is a sliced run. The clips the run is PLANNED to be cut into: the engine's own trajectory simulated with on-time ticks and full fills, not a restatement of duration_sec / interval_sec. It is an intention, not a record: the runner re-sizes each clip from what is left and the time left, so ordinary poll latency alone changes later sizes and can merge the last clips, with no book movement involved. Null when the run could not be planned. On both venues the planned sizes add up to the armed size: a clip that would leave a remainder too small to post is either cut so the remainder can still be posted, or carries that remainder itself — when no such split exists, or when no later clip would run before end_at. They sum to LESS only when what is left at the end is itself under the venue minimum (the market's share minimum or $1 of value on Polymarket, $0.90 of value on predict.fun, at the price the clip is signed at); that remainder is not posted.

average_price.description: Volume-weighted price of everything known to have filled AS OF THIS RESPONSE, before the venue's fee (the fee is charged inside the exchange's settlement transfer and is not reported in this response). Null when nothing has filled (a record-only placement, a resting clip) AND null on a fill whose price the venue's placement answer did not state. Not a quote and not an estimate: if it carries a number, that number was matched.

first_clip.description: TWAP ONLY, and only when this deployment places clip 1 inside the placement request: what happened to that clip, in the same field names a MARKET fill uses. `status` is `resting` (accepted, nothing matched yet — `filled_size` is "0" and that is a measurement), `filled` (some of it matched immediately), or `pending` (still in flight when the request's budget ran out, so the clip MAY be live — "0" is a floor, not a fact). `pending` is never an error: poll GET /v2/trade/strategies, which is where the runner reconciles it. Absent means the record was written and the runner places clip 1 on its next tick, which is the behaviour every earlier release had. `size` is the size the venue holds (its own echo once read, else the clip rounded down to the 2 decimals the order is signed at); `price` is the price the clip was POSTED at, as the venue echoes it, and null until the venue has been read; `average_price` is the matched price before fees, or null when the venue did not state it.

post.summary: Withdraw collateral to an external address
post.description: Transfers collateral out to an external address. Requires the trade.withdraw scope. Idempotency-Key required. Each venue returns its own collateral on its own chain: on polymarket, pUSD from the bound user's deposit wallet on Polygon; on predictfun, an ERC20 transfer from the user's EOA on BNB Chain, defaulting to the venue collateral (USDT-BEP20) when no token is given. Send to an address you control on that venue's chain. Treat STATE_PENDING, a 502 and a timeout alike as an indeterminate outcome, and note what transaction_hash does and does not tell you: it proves the transfer was SUBMITTED to the chain, not that it was mined or that it succeeded. Confirm it on chain before treating a withdrawal as final. While the key's retention window lasts, a retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key replays the stored response and transfers nothing again — but that is not a blanket guarantee. While the first request is still running you get 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT; a key whose request never finished gets 502 IDEMPOTENCY_INDETERMINATE; and once the retention window has passed the same string is a NEW key and WILL withdraw again. That window is 24h by default but is configurable and may be shorter, so treat it as an operational setting rather than a number to build on. Never mint a fresh key to get past an indeterminate result. To settle an indeterminate withdrawal, look up transaction_hash on chain — that is the authoritative check. On polymarket, a withdrawal made through THIS endpoint DOES appear in /activity?type=WITHDRAWAL: Polymarket's indexer does not classify it (it is a plain token transfer), so we serve it from our own record of the transfer, merged into the first page and marked `source: "ledger"`. Rows reconstructed from before we kept transaction hashes carry `source: "backfill"` and a null transaction_hash. On predictfun /activity still reports trades only — the merge is polymarket-only today, so a predictfun withdrawal will NOT show up there. A response carrying no transaction_hash at all is rare — the request refuses to broadcast once too little of its deadline remains. If it happens, contact support rather than reissuing. Bravado may hold a record of the transfer, but that is NOT guaranteed: a submit that fails ambiguously never produces a hash to record. Reissuing is the one action that can transfer twice.

post.summary: Preview what a MARKET order would be bounded at
post.description:
Read-only. Returns, for each of 300/500/1000/2000 bps, the EXACT limit price we would sign — from the same function the executor uses, so the quote and the order cannot disagree. Nothing is placed and no state is stored.

`worst_price` and `slippage_bps` are both returned on purpose: send the bps on a MARKET to accept a bound RELATIVE to the touch at submit time, or send `worst_price` as a LIMIT to commit to that absolute number. They are different promises and this endpoint does not choose between them.

The book moves between this read and your submit. A quote does not remove `SLIPPAGE_EXCEEDED` — it turns it from a surprise into a condition your user accepted and that did not hold.

token_id.description: Venue-native outcome token id — a decimal string on both venues, 77–78 digits (a uint256). Constrained because it reaches market lookups that interpolate it, and an id carrying query syntax was measured turning such a lookup into a different question (#973).

venue.description: Defaults to polymarket.

read_at.description: Epoch ms of the single book read this whole response derives from. The book moves; use this to age out what you showed the user.

tick.description: The market's own price tick. On predictfun it is per market (0.01 or 0.001, from the venue's decimalPrecision), not one value for the venue.

slippage_bps.description: Send this on a MARKET order to get the bound below. On predictfun it does not move the signed price today: every rung is the touch.

worst_price.description: The EXACT limit we would sign at this slippage_bps, from the same function the executor uses. Send it as a LIMIT price to commit to an absolute number instead of a relative bound. On the market's own grid (`book_at_read.tick`). On predictfun a MARKET is signed AT the touch (touch-or-nothing today, api#1385), so this is the touch on every rung.

ticks_from_touch.description: Distance from the touch in the market's own ticks. 0 means the bound is the touch itself — the order fills at the touch or not at all.

recommended_slippage_bps.description: The lowest rung that buys any room beyond the touch on THIS book, or NULL when no rung buys any. Null is not an error and not a default: at the edges of the price range (a sell at the lowest level, a buy at the highest) a MARKET cannot be widened into room the price range does not contain, so there is no bps worth recommending. Send a LIMIT at `worst_price` instead. Elsewhere a rung whose bps buy less than one tick is set 2 ticks from the touch (the tick floor, polymarket), so it does buy room.

get.description: Returns the integration, binding, api key, wallet (EOA + Safe), and the builder code resolved for this key. Useful as the first call after onboarding to verify credentials and inspect quotas. onboarding_status is per venue: with ?venue=predictfun — or under /v2/trade/predictfun/account — it reports predict.fun readiness instead of the Polygon pUSD allowance. Addresses here are chain-specific: safe_address is the Polymarket proxy on Polygon, while predict.fun collateral (USDT-BEP20 on BNB Chain) must be sent to the EOA instead. Read the safe_address field description before building a deposit flow.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list. On this endpoint it selects which venue's onboarding_status is reported; the wallet block is unchanged and still describes the Polymarket accounts.

eoa_address.description: The end user's externally owned account — a keypair, so the same value on every EVM chain. Carries no chain because it needs none. Do not build a deposit flow from this field: use venues[], where each address comes with the chain and assets it accepts.

safe_address.description: Addresses are chain-specific. safe_address identifies the user's Polymarket proxy on Polygon, and is NULL whenever the requested venue does not trade through a Safe — on predict.fun it is always null, because that venue trades from the EOA and no Safe exists there. Never use it as a deposit address for predict.fun: that collateral is USDT-BEP20 on BNB Chain and goes to the EOA. Bravado does not support recovery of funds sent to safe_address on BNB Chain, and recovery may be impossible; design your flow on the assumption that the loss is final. Prefer venues[] over this field — it labels every address with its chain.

chain.description: The chain these addresses are reported for — the requested venue's chain. Here so this block is machine-readable on its own: a client that never reads venues[] still cannot pair an address with the wrong network. It labels the context, not the keypair — eoa_address is the same account on every EVM chain, and this says which one these fields are answering about.

protocol_v2_status.description: Polymarket Protocol V2 markets only, and present only while Bravado trades them. Whether the user's wallet holds the ExchangeV3 approvals a V2 order needs: `ready`; `pending` — the first V2 order sets them (that order may need one retry), v1 trading is unaffected; `unknown` — the chain could not be read. Never gate v1 trading on it: `onboarding_status` is still the readiness to trade.

name.description: Human name, e.g. Polygon, BNB Smart Chain

trading_address.description: The address that trades on this venue. Null when it has not been derived yet — treat null as 'not ready', never as an empty address.

address_type.description: safe_proxy is a contract, deployed on this entry's chain; eoa is a keypair the user controls, which is the same account on any EVM chain. contract.description: ERC20 contract, or null for the chain's native coin.

venues.description: One entry per venue this partner may trade on, each self-contained: where to send money, on which chain, in which assets, and whether the user is ready there. Build deposit flows from this, not from the legacy wallet block — that block cannot express more than one chain.

get.description:
Open CLOB orders for the bound user, optionally filtered by ?token_id.

**Some of these orders are not yours.** A TWAP, iceberg or pegged record is worked by a runner that posts ordinary orders to the book, and they appear here like any other. `is_twap`, `is_iceberg` and `is_pegged` mark them, and `parent_strategy_id` names the record that owns each one — the id DELETE /v2/trade/strategies/{id} takes.

question.description: The market's question as Gamma words it. Note /positions carries a `title` from Polymarket's data-api instead: same market, two upstreams, so the WORDING can differ. Join on condition_id, not on the text.

outcome.description: Which side of the market this token is (e.g. "Yes"), derived from the token's position in the market's outcome list.

title.description: The market's name. Same string as `question` when it comes from the catalogue; a separate key because /positions and /activity already call it `title` and a client joining those surfaces should not have to learn two names.

outcome_index.description: Which outcome this token is, by position in the market's outcome list — the index `outcome` was read from.

venue.description: The venue this market was resolved on. Present so a client never has to infer it from the request it made.

market.description: Which market this order is on. NULL MEANS UNRESOLVED, never 'this token has no market': a market-data outage, an unknown token, and a venue we cannot look up all report null, and the order itself is unaffected either way. Resolved on BOTH venues from the market catalogue we index, so a predictfun order is named like a polymarket one. Best-effort by design: we will not fail a list of orders over a missing name, so treat it as a label and keep asset_id as the identity. A title here is never invented: a token the catalogue has not indexed, a row we cannot join to a condition id, and a failing lookup all come back null. A 500 here can only come from a producer bug that omits the field.

post.summary: Place an order (consolidated)
post.description: Single high-level order endpoint. `type` = LIMIT | MARKET | PEGGED | TWAP | ICEBERG. Optional `take_profit` / `stop_loss` brackets attach to a LIMIT/MARKET buy entry (placed after the entry; best-effort — a failing bracket is reported, not rolled back). Idempotency-Key required.

venue.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. predictfun is in limited availability and is not at feature parity — several order types and product families are unavailable there. See the Venues section for the supported list. On predictfun this endpoint accepts LIMIT, MARKET, TWAP and ICEBERG, and requires the partner venue entitlement.

symbol.description: Venue-native outcome token id — a decimal string on both venues. Constrained because it is interpolated into a market lookup: an id carrying query syntax was measured turning that lookup into a different question and returning an unrelated market (#973).

price.description: Decimal probability 0..1, e.g. "0.72" for 72¢ (NOT cents). Required for LIMIT / ICEBERG / TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS. Optional for TWAP (derived from the live top of book when omitted) and TRAILING_STOP (reference; execution.high_water_mark also works).

size.description: Shares. Required for LIMIT / ICEBERG / TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS / TRAILING_STOP and MARKET sell; for TWAP either size or quote_amount works.

quote_amount.description: US dollars. MARKET buy notional; TWAP: shares are derived from it at the limit price; PEGGED: accepted as an alias for budget_usdc.

time_in_force.description: LIMIT only. GTC (default) rests on the book (GTD when expiration is set). IOC fills whatever crosses immediately and cancels the remainder (Polymarket FAK) — the response reports the actual filled_size. FOK fills the full size instantly or cancels entirely. Incompatible with expiration. ON MARKET: a MARKET order is always FAK, so `IOC` is accepted and changes nothing, while `GTC` and `FOK` are REJECTED with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than silently ignored — neither can be honoured (a MARKET order never rests, and it is not all-or-nothing). PREDICTFUN: on a LIMIT only GTC, the default, is accepted; IOC and FOK are VENUE_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. On a MARKET, IOC is accepted there too: the venue cancels a MARKET that does not fill at the touch.

slippage_bps.description: MARKET only. How far from the top of book this order may fill, in basis points (100 = 1%). THE DEFAULT DIFFERS BY VENUE: 300 on polymarket, 100 on predictfun — same field, same 1-5000 range, so omitting it gives you a 3x tighter bound on predictfun. Send the value explicitly if you want one number across venues. The reference is the touch at submit time: the best BID for a sell, the best ASK for a buy — so on a sell it is a price FLOOR, and on a buy a price CEILING. Orders are FAK: the book fills what it can within the bound and the remainder is cancelled, so a partial fill is normal and `filled_size` reports what actually traded. If NOTHING fills within the bound the order is rejected with SLIPPAGE_EXCEEDED (422) and nothing trades — that is a race (the book emptied between our read and the match), not the ordinary outcome. Raising this widens your exposure; it cannot be disabled.

expiration.description: LIMIT and ICEBERG only. Unix seconds; 0 or omitted means GTC. Any other type (MARKET, TWAP, PEGGED, brackets, trailing) rejects it with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than accepting and ignoring it. Must be at least 10s in the future, and no later than 4102444800 (the GTC sentinel) — a larger value is what milliseconds look like where seconds were asked for; both fail with INVALID_BODY. The two types enforce it differently and the difference is worth designing around: on LIMIT the timestamp is signed INTO the order and enforced by the venue, so it holds exactly and even if we are unreachable. On ICEBERG it is a deadline for the STRATEGY, enforced by our runner on its next poll — the record is canceled and its live clip pulled shortly AFTER the timestamp, not at it.

condition_id.description: Optional. Omit it and we resolve the market from `symbol`. An EMPTY string used to be accepted and then failed every lookup silently, so the shape is pinned rather than merely non-empty.

offset_ticks.description: PEGGED: distance from the touch in CLOB ticks (1 tick = $0.001); 0 = passive at the touch.

budget_usdc.description: PEGGED buy budget in US dollars, top-level decimal string, e.g. "50". quote_amount is accepted as an alias.

price_floor.description: Decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (NOT cents). Two uses. PEGGED: the lowest price the runner will chase down to. TWAP SELL with no `price`: the limit every clip is priced against, so each clip fills at max(live touch, this) instead of being pinned to the touch at placement. With `execution.passive: true` a clip rests one tick INSIDE the touch (bestBid + tick), so that formula is off by a tick — the promise that we never cross your number holds in both modes, the arithmetic is exact only in the default one. Snapped protectively — a floor ceils to the cent above, never below your number. WHEN IT IS ACTING AS THE LIMIT it is also what your notional cap is measured against: the cap is `price x size` with no side branch, so a floor bounds a sell exactly as a ceiling bounds a buy. Send an explicit `price` and the cap is measured against that instead.

price_ceiling.description: Decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (NOT cents). Two uses. PEGGED: the highest price the runner will chase up to. TWAP BUY with no `price`: the limit every clip is priced against, so each clip fills at min(live touch, this) instead of being pinned to the touch at placement. With `execution.passive: true` a clip rests one tick INSIDE the touch (bestAsk - tick), so that formula is off by a tick — the promise that we never cross your number holds in both modes, the arithmetic is exact only in the default one. Snapped protectively — a ceiling floors to the cent below, never above your number. WHEN IT IS ACTING AS THE LIMIT it is also what your notional cap is measured against, since `size x ceiling` is the most the order can then spend — so an open ceiling consumes cap. Send an explicit `price` and the cap is measured against that instead.

duration_sec.description: TWAP total run length in seconds

passive.description: TWAP slice style. Default false: each slice takes the touch (buy at the best ask, sell at the best bid), never past your price, so it executes. True: rest one tick inside the touch and never cross — cheaper when it fills, but often it does not. Use it on long horizons.

low_water_mark.description: TRAILING_BUY starting reference price (decimal). Omit to let the engine seed it from the first ask it sees, which is what you want when arming at the current market.

price_ceiling.description: TRAILING_BUY ONLY. Hard cap, decimal probability strictly between 0 and 1 (`0.0` and `0.00` are zero, and are refused): if the ask gaps past it the entry does not fire at any price and the order stays armed for a cheaper ask. A TWAP reads price_ceiling at the TOP LEVEL of the order, not here — sending it inside `execution` on a TWAP is rejected with INVALID_BODY rather than ignored.

price_floor.description: NOT USED HERE, and rejected. A TWAP SELL reads price_floor at the TOP LEVEL of the order. This field exists only so that sending it in the wrong place fails loudly instead of being dropped.

quote_amount.description: NOT USED HERE, and rejected. MARKET buy, TWAP and PEGGED all read quote_amount at the TOP LEVEL of the order. This field exists only so that sending it in the wrong place fails loudly instead of being dropped.

size.description: Shares for this bracket (optional). Omitted or "0" = the whole entry; set a positive value to protect only part of the position.
Shares for this bracket (optional). Omitted or "0" = the whole entry; set a positive value to protect only part of the position.

status.description: The venue's word for the order when it was accepted. ALWAYS PRESENT: the empty string "" is the documented UNKNOWN (a predict.fun LIMIT: the venue's acceptance does not say whether it matched), not a missing field. Test === "", not truthiness. On a MARKET: "matched" = filled in full; "partially_filled" = filled, but at least 0.01 shares (sell) or $0.01 (buy) short of the request, the rest cancelled and nothing resting. A SUCCESS, not an error: treat it as one if you allow-list "matched" (added in #1396). "pending" (predict.fun MARKET) = the venue had not reported the fill when we answered; the final state can arrive later. Not a cancel and not a zero fill: do not place it again (#1412).

filled_size.description: Shares matched at acceptance. "" = UNKNOWN (a predict.fun LIMIT, whose acceptance carries no fill, and a predict.fun MARKET answered "pending"), never zero: reading "" as 0 or as absent is wrong. Reconcile from /orders/open or your fills.

remaining_size.description: What rests after acceptance. "" = UNKNOWN, same rule as filled_size.

planned_at.description: Unix seconds this clip is PLANNED for: clip 1 at created_at, clip k at created_at + (k-1) * interval_sec. Nominal — the runner places each clip on the first poll tick at or after its due time and never catches up, so later clips run late by the accumulated latency.

planned_size.description: Shares this clip is PLANNED at. Nominal: the runner re-sizes every clip from what is left and the time left, so late ticks and resting clips change later sizes and can merge the last clips. Reconcile fills through /orders/open and GET /v2/trade/strategies.

clip_plan.description: TWAP ONLY — absent on every other type, so its presence says the placement is a sliced run. The clips the run is PLANNED to be cut into: the engine's own trajectory simulated with on-time ticks and full fills, not a restatement of duration_sec / interval_sec. It is an intention, not a record: the runner re-sizes each clip from what is left and the time left, so ordinary poll latency alone changes later sizes and can merge the last clips, with no book movement involved. Null when the run could not be planned. On both venues the planned sizes add up to the armed size: a clip that would leave a remainder too small to post is either cut so the remainder can still be posted, or carries that remainder itself — when no such split exists, or when no later clip would run before end_at. They sum to LESS only when what is left at the end is itself under the venue minimum (the market's share minimum or $1 of value on Polymarket, $0.90 of value on predict.fun, at the price the clip is signed at); that remainder is not posted.

average_price.description: Volume-weighted price of everything known to have filled AS OF THIS RESPONSE, before the venue's fee (the fee is charged inside the exchange's settlement transfer and is not reported in this response). Null when nothing has filled (a record-only placement, a resting clip) AND null on a fill whose price the venue's placement answer did not state. Not a quote and not an estimate: if it carries a number, that number was matched.

first_clip.description: TWAP ONLY, and only when this deployment places clip 1 inside the placement request: what happened to that clip, in the same field names a MARKET fill uses. `status` is `resting` (accepted, nothing matched yet — `filled_size` is "0" and that is a measurement), `filled` (some of it matched immediately), or `pending` (still in flight when the request's budget ran out, so the clip MAY be live — "0" is a floor, not a fact). `pending` is never an error: poll GET /v2/trade/strategies, which is where the runner reconciles it. Absent means the record was written and the runner places clip 1 on its next tick, which is the behaviour every earlier release had. `size` is the size the venue holds (its own echo once read, else the clip rounded down to the 2 decimals the order is signed at); `price` is the price the clip was POSTED at, as the venue echoes it, and null until the venue has been read; `average_price` is the matched price before fees, or null when the venue did not state it.

symbol.description: Venue-native outcome token id — a decimal string on both venues. Constrained because it is interpolated into a market lookup: an id carrying query syntax was measured turning that lookup into a different question and returning an unrelated market (#973).

status.description: The venue's word for the order when it was accepted. ALWAYS PRESENT: the empty string "" is the documented UNKNOWN (a predict.fun LIMIT: the venue's acceptance does not say whether it matched), not a missing field. Test === "", not truthiness. On a MARKET: "matched" = filled in full; "partially_filled" = filled, but at least 0.01 shares (sell) or $0.01 (buy) short of the request, the rest cancelled and nothing resting. A SUCCESS, not an error: treat it as one if you allow-list "matched" (added in #1396). "pending" (predict.fun MARKET) = the venue had not reported the fill when we answered; the final state can arrive later. Not a cancel and not a zero fill: do not place it again (#1412).

post.summary: Withdraw collateral to an external address
post.description: Transfers collateral out to an external address. Requires the trade.withdraw scope. Idempotency-Key required. Each venue returns its own collateral on its own chain: on polymarket, pUSD from the bound user's deposit wallet on Polygon; on predictfun, an ERC20 transfer from the user's EOA on BNB Chain, defaulting to the venue collateral (USDT-BEP20) when no token is given. Send to an address you control on that venue's chain. Treat STATE_PENDING, a 502 and a timeout alike as an indeterminate outcome, and note what transaction_hash does and does not tell you: it proves the transfer was SUBMITTED to the chain, not that it was mined or that it succeeded. Confirm it on chain before treating a withdrawal as final. While the key's retention window lasts, a retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key replays the stored response and transfers nothing again — but that is not a blanket guarantee. While the first request is still running you get 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT; a key whose request never finished gets 502 IDEMPOTENCY_INDETERMINATE; and once the retention window has passed the same string is a NEW key and WILL withdraw again. That window is 24h by default but is configurable and may be shorter, so treat it as an operational setting rather than a number to build on. Never mint a fresh key to get past an indeterminate result. To settle an indeterminate withdrawal, look up transaction_hash on chain — that is the authoritative check. On polymarket, a withdrawal made through THIS endpoint DOES appear in /activity?type=WITHDRAWAL: Polymarket's indexer does not classify it (it is a plain token transfer), so we serve it from our own record of the transfer, merged into the first page and marked `source: "ledger"`. Rows reconstructed from before we kept transaction hashes carry `source: "backfill"` and a null transaction_hash. On predictfun /activity still reports trades only — the merge is polymarket-only today, so a predictfun withdrawal will NOT show up there. A response carrying no transaction_hash at all is rare — the request refuses to broadcast once too little of its deadline remains. If it happens, contact support rather than reissuing. Bravado may hold a record of the transfer, but that is NOT guaranteed: a submit that fails ambiguously never produces a hash to record. Reissuing is the one action that can transfer twice.

token.description: ERC20 token contract to withdraw (0x + 40 hex), on the venue's own chain. Omit to withdraw that venue's default collateral — pUSD on polymarket, USDT-BEP20 on predictfun. Pass any token address on that chain to recover that asset instead.

get.description: What the bound user can pull out on a venue. On polymarket: ERC20 holdings of the Polygon deposit wallet (via Allium), zero balances dropped. On ?venue=predictfun: USDT-BEP20 (collateral) and native BNB (gas) held by the user's EOA on BNB Chain — gas is listed because that wallet pays for its own approvals, cancels and redeems, so draining it strands the positions. IMPORTANT: `balance` is the TOTAL held, not the spendable amount. Neither venue escrows collateral for a resting order, so anything committed to an open buy is still counted here. Pass ?include_locked=true to measure it into `locked_in_open_orders` (one extra venue call); otherwise that field is null, meaning NOT MEASURED rather than zero.

parameters.name: venue
parameters.description: Selects the trading venue. Default polymarket. The address read differs by venue: polymarket reports the Polygon deposit wallet, predictfun the user's own EOA on BNB Chain.

parameters.name: include_locked
parameters.description: Measure locked_in_open_orders. OFF by default because it costs a venue API call against a rate limit shared with the strategy engines. When off, locked_in_open_orders is null — which means NOT MEASURED, not zero.

token.description: ERC20 contract address, or null for the chain's NATIVE coin (BNB on predictfun). Null is not an error — it means there is no contract to call.

role.description: collateral funds trading on this venue; gas pays for the wallet's own transactions (on predictfun it pays its own approvals, cancels and redeems, so withdrawing all of it strands the positions); other is anything else the wallet holds and can recover — a legacy collateral, an airdrop, dust. Do not size trades off `other`.

locked_in_open_orders.description: Human-decimal amount of this asset committed to resting orders, or NULL when not measured (see include_locked). Neither venue escrows collateral for a resting order — it is pulled at match against an allowance — so this amount is STILL inside `balance`. Subtract it before offering a withdraw-all, or the withdraw succeeds and the orders fail at match. Null must never be read as zero.
